lead: The team continued to play although it was raining heavily.
hint: carry on + -ing (phrasal verb) + despite + noun (concession)

lead: A professional photographer took our family photos last month.
hint: have + object + past participle (causative)

lead: Sarah was very proud of her exam results.
hint: take pride in (adj→noun word-class shift + collocation + preposition change)

lead: People think the company has lost millions this year.
hint: passive reporting verb + perfect infinitive

lead: There was no point in waiting any longer for the bus.
gapped: It ______________________ any longer for the bus.
hint: it's not worth + -ing (futility expression equivalence)

lead: We couldn't get to the airport because of the heavy snow.
hint: prevent + object + from + -ing (causal subject swap + verb pattern)

lead: 'I can't think of a solution to this problem,' said David.
gapped: David said he was unable to ______________________ to the problem.
hint: come up with (phrasal verb = think of) + reported speech

lead: I regret not making more effort at school.
hint: wish + past perfect (past regret) + effort→tried (word-class shift)

lead: Nobody has claimed the lost wallet yet.
hint: present perfect passive (negative)

lead: The water was too cold for the children to swim in.
gapped: The water was ______________________ the children to swim in.
hint: not + adj + enough + for (too cold → not warm enough: antonym + enough structure)

lead: I didn't know about the meeting, so I didn't attend.
gapped: Had I known about the meeting, I ______________________ without a second thought.
hint: type 3 conditional + inverted form (had I known → would have + pp)

lead: It took the builders six months to finish the house.
hint: spend + time + -ing (it takes → spend: time expression shift)

lead: The police are investigating the robbery.
hint: phrasal verb (look into = investigate) + present continuous passive

lead: You can use my laptop if you are careful with it.
gapped: You can use my laptop ______________________ careful with it.
hint: as long as = provided that / if (conditional)

lead: It was foolish of Tom to leave his bag on the train.
gapped: Tom ______________________ his bag on the train.
hint: should not have + past participle (past criticism/regret)

lead: Although she had studied all night, she failed the exam.
gapped: She failed the exam ______________________ all night.
hint: in spite of + -ing (concession: although clause → prepositional phrase)

lead: Lisa's English is improving more quickly than expected.
gapped: Lisa is ______________________ expected with her English.
hint: make progress (collocation) + comparative + than

lead: 'You copied my answers during the test!' said Maria to James.
gapped: Maria ______________________ her answers during the test.
hint: accuse + object + of + -ing (reporting verb pattern)

lead: I find it very difficult to concentrate when it's noisy.
hint: have difficulty + -ing (word-class shift: difficult→difficulty)

lead: 'You should stop eating so much sugar,' the doctor told me.
hint: advise + object + to-infinitive + phrasal verb (give up + -ing)

lead: People believe the painting is worth over ten million pounds.
gapped: The painting ______________________ over ten million pounds.
hint: passive reporting verb + to be + worth

lead: The heavy traffic meant that we missed our flight.
gapped: We missed our flight ______________________ the heavy traffic.
hint: as a result of (formal cause expression, like due to/because of)

lead: Emma used to walk to school, but now her mother drives her.
hint: no longer + present simple (used to → no longer: past habit ended)

lead: They postponed the football match because of the bad weather.
gapped: The football match ______________________ the bad weather.
hint: put off = postpone (phrasal verb passive + because of)

lead: I will never forget meeting the President in 2019.
hint: remember + -ing (memory of past event; never forget → always remember)

lead: There isn't much chance of the weather improving today.
hint: be likely to + infinitive (chance → likely: probability expression)

lead: I want you to speak more quietly, please.
hint: would rather + different subject + past simple (request/preference)

lead: The judges will consider your previous experience.
gapped: Your previous experience ______________________ by the judges.
hint: take into account (collocation) + future passive

lead: At first it was strange for me to live alone.
gapped: It took me a while to ______________________ alone.
hint: get used to + -ing (becoming accustomed to a new situation)

lead: It was such a long journey that we all fell asleep.
gapped: The journey ______________________ we all fell asleep.
hint: such + a + adj + noun → so + adj + that (result clause)

lead: Jack refused to accept the job they offered him.
hint: turn down = refuse/reject (phrasal verb + reported action)

lead: The university awarded Maria a scholarship last year.
hint: passive with double object (indirect object becomes subject)

lead: It annoys me that my brother always leaves the door open.
hint: wish + subject + wouldn't + base (wish for behaviour change)

lead: Almost all the tickets for the concert have been sold.
hint: hardly any + noun (quantifier shift); 'left' is fixed outside the gap so only one completion fits

lead: She spoke quietly because she didn't want to wake the baby.
hint: in order not to + base (negative purpose clause)

lead: The children should really go to bed now - it's very late.
hint: it's high time + subject + past simple (urgent recommendation)

lead: You are welcome to contact me if you need any help.
gapped: Please feel free to ______________________ if you need any help.
hint: get in touch with (collocation = contact) + conditional

lead: The thick fog resulted in the flight being delayed.
hint: due to + noun phrase (resulted in → due to: formal cause expression)

lead: 'I'll pay for everyone's dinner,' said Carlos.
hint: insist on + -ing (reporting verb + dependent preposition)

lead: If you don't leave now, you'll miss the last train.
gapped: You'll miss the last train ______________________ now.
hint: unless = if not (conditional)

lead: Elena started learning Japanese three years ago and is still learning it.
hint: present perfect continuous (started + still doing → has been + -ing)

lead: That was the worst meal I have ever had in a restaurant.
hint: superlative → comparative with never (worst → never worse)

lead: She is not old enough to travel abroad by herself.
gapped: She is not old enough to travel abroad ______________________ yet.
hint: on one's own = by oneself (fixed expression)

lead: 'Don't swim in the river - it's very dangerous,' said the guide.
hint: warn + object + not to + base (reported prohibition/advice)

lead: I'm sure Tom didn't read my email because he hasn't replied.
hint: cannot have + pp (negative past deduction) + because

lead: Everyone says Julia looks exactly like her mother.
hint: take after = resemble/look like (phrasal verb ↔ formal verb)

lead: You should book your tickets now - the price will go up soon.
hint: the + comparative...the + comparative (double comparative)

lead: I haven't spoken to my cousin for ages.
hint: it's been ages since + past simple (time expression shift)

lead: I haven't decided yet whether to accept the job offer.
hint: make up one's mind (collocation = decide) + about

lead: We enjoyed the holiday even though the hotel was disappointing.
hint: despite + noun phrase (even though + clause → despite + noun)

lead: 'I'm very sorry I arrived late,' said the teacher.
hint: apologise for + -ing (reporting verb + dependent preposition)

lead: I bought a new pen, but there were plenty in the drawer.
hint: needn't have + pp (action was done but unnecessary)

lead: The suitcase was too heavy for me to carry up the stairs.
gapped: The suitcase was ______________________ carry it up the stairs.
hint: too + adj + to → so + adj + that + couldn't (degree + result)

lead: I can't wait to see you next weekend.
gapped: I am really ______________________ you next weekend.
hint: look forward to + -ing (anticipation expression)

lead: People say this restaurant serves the best pasta in town.
gapped: This restaurant ______________________ the best pasta in town.
hint: passive reporting verb + present infinitive (people say → is said to)

lead: It took Rachel a long time to recover from her illness.
gapped: It took Rachel a long time to ______________________ illness.
hint: get over = recover from (phrasal verb ↔ formal verb)

lead: Several passengers complained about the noise on the train.
gapped: Several passengers ______________________ the noise on the train.
hint: make a complaint about (verb→noun collocation shift)

lead: I have never tasted anything so delicious before.
gapped: This is the ______________________ anything so delicious.
hint: it's the first time + present perfect (never → first time)

lead: I tried hard and in the end I was able to solve the puzzle.
gapped: After a lot of effort, I ______________________ the puzzle.
hint: managed to = was able to (with effort/achievement implication)

lead: It's a shame I don't live closer to the beach.
hint: wish + past simple (present unreal regret)

lead: We have no milk left - someone needs to go to the shop.
hint: run out of (phrasal verb = have none left)

lead: Tom and his brother are not very similar to each other.
gapped: Tom and his brother do not ______________________ each other.
hint: have something in common with (collocation = be similar)

lead: I can't afford a new car because I don't earn enough.
gapped: If I earned more money, I ______________________ car.
hint: type 2 conditional: if + past simple → could + base

lead: 'Well done on passing your driving test, Amy!' said her father.
hint: congratulate + object + on + -ing (reporting verb pattern)

lead: There are not as many students in this class as last year.
hint: not as many → fewer + noun (comparative quantifier for countable)

lead: I really regret not applying for that job.
hint: if only + past perfect (strong past regret)

lead: You should make the most of this opportunity while it lasts.
gapped: You should ______________________ this opportunity while it lasts.
hint: take advantage of (collocation = make the most of)

lead: Although the exam was very difficult, most students passed.
gapped: The exam was very difficult; ______________________ managed to pass.
hint: although + clause → sentence + however (concession linker shift)

lead: 'I didn't break the window,' said the boy.
gapped: The boy ______________________ , even though everyone had seen him do it.
hint: deny + -ing (reporting verb pattern)

lead: All the students in the school admire Mr Harris enormously.
gapped: All the students in the school ______________________ as a teacher.
hint: look up to = admire (phrasal verb ↔ formal verb)

lead: When we arrived at the station, the train had already left.
gapped: By ______________________ the station, the train had already left.
hint: by the time + past simple (time clause with past perfect main clause)

lead: I didn't bring an umbrella, so I got wet.
gapped: I ______________________ wet because I didn't bring an umbrella.
hint: end up + -ing (unintentional-action structure: an unplanned outcome, not a deliberate one)

lead: Working long hours is not a problem for Anna - she has always done it.
hint: be used to + -ing (accustomed to: familiarity through habit)

lead: Over 500 runners participated in this year's marathon.
hint: take part in (collocation = participate)

lead: David broke the vase accidentally while he was cleaning the shelf.
gapped: David ______________________ the vase while he was cleaning the shelf.
hint: didn't mean to + base (unintentional-action structure: accidentally = without meaning to)

lead: Would it be OK if I opened the window?
hint: would you mind if + past simple (polite request structure)

lead: Laura stopped eating meat two years ago and hasn't eaten it since.
hint: give up + -ing (phrasal verb = stop doing permanently)

lead: The moment the rain stopped, the children went outside to play.
gapped: The children went outside to play ______________________ stopped.
hint: as soon as (time conjunction = the moment)

lead: My neighbour looked after our cat while we were on holiday.
gapped: My neighbour ______________________ while we were on holiday.
hint: take care of (collocation = look after)

lead: 'Why don't we eat out tonight?' said Laura.
hint: suggest + -ing (reporting verb pattern for suggestions)

lead: I'm sure they are enjoying themselves - listen to them laughing.
hint: must be + -ing (present continuous deduction: certainty about a current action)

lead: This year's exam was less difficult than last year's.
hint: less + adj → not as + adj + as (comparative equivalence)

lead: Rachel established her own company at the age of 25.
hint: set up = establish (phrasal verb ↔ formal verb)

lead: If you don't leave now, you will be late for the meeting.
gapped: You ______________________ or you will be late for the meeting.
hint: had better + base (strong advice with implied consequence)

lead: Trying to change his mind is pointless - he won't listen.
hint: it's no use + -ing (equivalence: pointless → no use)

lead: When I was young, my father often took us fishing on Sundays.
gapped: When I was young, my father ______________________ on Sundays.
hint: would + base (past repeated action - not states)

lead: 'Don't forget to lock the back door, Sam,' said his mother.
hint: remind + object + to-infinitive (reporting verb pattern)

lead: The committee hasn't decided anything about the new building yet.
gapped: There has been ______________________ made about the new building yet.
hint: there has been no + noun (make a decision collocation); fixed singular 'has been' anchors the noun as singular

lead: She left the room and didn't say a single word.
gapped: She left the room ______________________ , which surprised everyone.
hint: without + -ing (negative circumstance: didn't say → without saying)

lead: They don't let children under 12 into the cinema after 9 pm.
gapped: Children under 12 ______________________ the cinema after 9 pm.
hint: be allowed to/into (passive permission: don't let → not allowed)

lead: 'My car stopped working on the way to the office,' said Paul.
gapped: Paul said that his car had ______________________ to the office.
hint: break down = stop working (phrasal verb) + reported speech tense shift

lead: My sister doesn't enjoy swimming as much as I do.
gapped: My sister is ______________________ swimming as I am.
hint: keen on = enjoy/like (adjective + preposition) + not as...as

lead: Perhaps Kate left her keys at the office.
hint: might have + pp (past possibility/speculation)

lead: Ben's French has improved a lot since he moved to Paris.
gapped: Ben has ______________________ since he moved to Paris.
hint: make progress (collocation: improve → make progress)

lead: The last time I saw Rachel was at her wedding.
hint: present perfect + since (last time → haven't + since)

lead: I'll lend you my car on one condition - you fill it up with petrol.
gapped: I'll lend you my car ______________________ it up with petrol.
hint: provided that = on condition that / if (conditional)

lead: I was very surprised by the news of their engagement.
gapped: The news of their engagement ______________________ me.
hint: come as a surprise to (collocation: was surprised → came as a surprise)

lead: I'm sure the exam wasn't easy because everyone looked worried.
gapped: The exam ______________________ because everyone looked worried.
hint: cannot have been + adj (past negative deduction)

lead: 'I'll help you carry those heavy bags,' Tom said to me.
hint: offer + to-infinitive (reporting verb pattern: volunteering)

lead: If you practise more, you will improve faster.
hint: the + comparative...the + comparative (double comparative)

lead: Someone has recently painted our house.
gapped: We have recently ______________________ in a pale blue colour.
hint: have + object + past participle (causative: present perfect)

lead: I can't tolerate the noise from the building site any longer.
gapped: I can no longer ______________________ the noise from the building site.
hint: put up with = tolerate (phrasal verb ↔ formal verb)

lead: The students shared the work of cleaning the classroom every week.
gapped: The students ______________________ the classroom every week.
hint: take turns + -ing (collocation: shared the work → took turns)

lead: I didn't study medicine because my grades weren't good enough.
gapped: If my grades had been better, I ______________________ medicine.
hint: type 3 conditional: if + past perfect → would have + pp (past hypothetical)

lead: Police believe the burglar entered through a back window.
gapped: The burglar ______________________ through a back window.
hint: passive reporting verb + perfect infinitive (believe → is thought to have)

lead: The council will continue with the building work as planned.
gapped: The council will ______________________ the building work.
hint: go ahead with = proceed/continue as planned (phrasal verb)

lead: I tried as hard as I could but I still failed the test.
gapped: I ______________________ I still failed the test.
hint: do one's best (collocation = try as hard as possible)

lead: We didn't have enough evidence to prove he was guilty.
gapped: ______________________ evidence meant we could not prove he was guilty.
hint: lack of + noun (not enough → lack of: noun phrase restructure)

lead: I'm sure you were very tired after the long journey.
hint: must have been + adj (past positive deduction)

lead: 'I'll definitely finish the report by Friday,' said Jenny.
hint: promise + to-infinitive (reporting verb pattern)

lead: I couldn't find the answer to the last maths problem.
hint: work out = calculate/solve (phrasal verb ↔ formal expression)

lead: We had a wonderful picnic although the weather was terrible.
gapped: We had a wonderful picnic ______________________ weather.
hint: despite + noun phrase (although + clause → despite + noun)

lead: I am not planning to change my mind about this.
hint: have no intention of + -ing (collocation: not planning → no intention of)

lead: He spoke very quietly because he didn't want to disturb anyone.
hint: so as not to + base (negative purpose clause)

lead: We didn't have enough money to go on holiday last summer.
hint: can't afford + to-infinitive (not enough money → can't afford)

lead: She made no effort to improve her work.
hint: make effort (collocation) + any (negative context) + to-infinitive

lead: 'I was at home all evening,' the suspect told the police.
gapped: The suspect ______________________ at home all evening.
hint: claim + to have been (reporting verb + perfect infinitive)

lead: I sent the email to the wrong person by mistake.
gapped: I sent the email to the wrong person ______________________ , and now I feel embarrassed.
hint: without meaning to = by mistake / accidentally (unintentional-action structure)

lead: No matter what the weather is like, she always goes for a run.
gapped: She always goes for a run ______________________ weather.
hint: regardless of (= no matter what: concession/indifference)

lead: People blamed the goalkeeper for losing the match.
hint: blame + object + for + -ing (passive reporting: people blamed → was blamed for)
